extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (Horizon Europe), in particular applicants submitting via NTNU
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing Part B of an MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship (Horizon Europe) application, covering methodology, work packages, open science, supervision, training, data management and impact. Targeted at applicants drafting their proposal text and plan (including Gantt and deliverables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall methodology — coherence between objectives and work packages
rubrics_metrics.description: The methodology/approach to achieve your research objectives is typically presented as work packages (broken down into tasks) ... Your work packages must correspond clearly with your research objectives established under section 1.1. Many lower-scoring proposals lack coherence between the objectives and WPs. This can typically arise because of a difference in the number of WPs and objectives, without indicating or describing how they are connected (we recommend a 1:1 relationship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start subsection 1.2 with a brief overview of your workplan (visual tool like a PERT diagram). The visual aid should show interplay between WPs and arrows must indicate identifiable flows of results (data/knowledge). Without a clear and convincing overview, the project risks being judged fragmented (a collection of largely independent small projects). Do not introduce new objective-defining information in WP descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work package descriptions — headings, tasks, naming and interrelation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each WP description should have a heading (WP1 - heading text) explaining the main action/purpose of the WP (linking back to its corresponding objective defined in subsection 1.1). The workflow within the WPs should be organised as tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the number of tasks is manageable (about 2-3 tasks are common per WP). Name tasks consistently (e.g. T1.1, T1.2). Use this WP/task nomenclature throughout the proposal (including the Gantt chart). For each WP, state the main expected results and how they feed into/are related to the other WPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods detail and justification (feasibility & appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must describe and explain the assumptions that underpin your work; and explain how this will enable you to deliver your project's objectives. Describe the methods including the concepts and models you will be using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what kind of data will be collected and how much, who/what will be included, and how the data will be analysed. The evaluator must be able to assess whether your methods/approach are feasible and appropriate to answer your research objectives/questions. Justify your choice of methods/approach in a few lines and make clear your expertise and that of your supervisor(s). Where relevant, define benchmarks of success for parameters of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI methods — describe techniques and robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: When including elements of AI in your proposal, techniques and robustness of the methods must be well described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be very descriptive to convince evaluators of feasibility — explain algorithms/approaches, validation, failure modes and why chosen techniques are appropriate. Failure to describe robustness is a common weakness in lower-scoring proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the risks/challenges that you might encounter and indicate how you will mitigate them. Research that pushes beyond state of the art will include riskier conceptual or operational elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid trivial risks; focus on conceptual risks (e.g. hypothesis falsified) or risks related to new methodology. Use promising preliminary data to increase feasibility. Indicate risk probability (optionally in WP heading). Preferably place riskier parts toward the end of the work plan so the project is not jeopardised early. Milestones may correspond to overcoming key risks/challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of methods and disciplines / interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how your project incorporates an interdisciplinary approach: what knowledge or tools/methods you are combining from different disciplines and why this is necessary for addressing your objectives/research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain two-way knowledge transfer (e.g. applicant brings a complementary disciplinary perspective to the supervisor). If research brings together knowledge from different sectors (e.g. a non-academic placement), highlight it. Under Horizon Europe you MUST provide a justification if you do not consider an interdisciplinary approach necessary (evaluators prefer interdisciplinary projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender dimension and other diversity aspects in the research content
rubrics_metrics.description: All Horizon Europe-funded projects must actively integrate the gender dimension in the content of their planned research. You MUST provide a justification if you do not consider gender/diversity aspects relevant for your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why gender and other diversity aspects are relevant and how you will address them. Examples: will women and men respond differently? Have you questioned gender assumptions? For medicine/health, consider differential effects and include sex-balanced design/analysis if applicable. Note: this section is about the gender dimension in research content, not about institutional gender policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science practices — mandatory expectations and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizon Europe funded-projects are expected to pursue ambitious open science practices. Open Science is an approach based on open cooperative work and systematic sharing of knowledge and tools as early and widely as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You MUST justify if open science practices are not appropriate (this may lower score). Do not describe outreach here (use Section 2 Impact). Evaluators are instructed to reward applicants who incorporate well-described recommended open science practices, but be realistic and explain how practices are adapted to your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access (OA) to scientific publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Access (OA) to scientific publications is mandatory: peer-reviewed academic publications must be made freely available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how you will publish OA: Gold OA (publishing in OA journal/platform; often with APCs) or Green OA (self-archiving the Author Accepted Manuscript in a repository). NTNU recommends CC BY 4.0 and requires depositing the published version or AAM in NTNU Open. Describe route, likely journals/platforms and how institutional support (e.g. library covering APCs) will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible management of research data and other research outputs (FAIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research data management must follow the FAIR principles ('Findability', 'Accessibility', 'Interoperability' and 'Reusability'). You must explain how data/research outputs will be managed in line with FAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Data Management Plan (DMP) is a compulsory Deliverable due by month 6 and must be included in the Gantt chart. In the proposal demonstrate that you have reflected on RDM: (1) outline what data/outputs will be generated (be specific), (2) say how you will make them available in line with FAIR (which repositories, persistent identifiers, file formats, standardised metadata), (3) describe terms of reuse and licensing. Prefer discipline-specific trustworthy repositories; if none, use NTNU DataverseNO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research outputs access and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information about the research outputs/tools/instruments needed to validate the conclusions of scientific publications or to validate/re-use research data, and ensure digital or physical access to such results unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what outputs (software, code, data, instruments) are needed for validation, how they will be shared, and any justified exceptions. Be specific about repositories, formats and preservation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data licensing and access conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the terms under which your data can be used; assign a licence so third parties know permitted uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to make data 'as open as possible' (e.g. CC0 or CC BY). If access must be restricted (e.g. sensitive personal data), explain why and describe access procedures. State licensing choices and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of supervision — arrangements and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors should be clearly identified; arrangements must define that proposed supervisors are sufficiently expert, have time, knowledge, experience, expertise and commitment to offer appropriate support and necessary feedback mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how supervision will ensure progress and review procedures. Applicants are encouraged to follow MSCA Guidelines on Supervision. Describe interaction frequency (tip: meet weekly or bi-weekly rather than monthly) and feedback mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and experience of the supervisor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear that the supervisor(s) has/have relevant scientific qualifications and experience with supervision of PhD and/or postdoctoral researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe supervisor's track record as a leading, internationally recognised researcher (network, publications, patents, funding, project management, spin-offs, editorial work, governmental advice). State experience with the research topic/methods and how supervisors' expertise is complementary. Give numbers of PhDs/postdocs supervised and outcomes (e.g. careers of former group members). For secondments/non-academic placements or Global Fellowships, include similar detail for those supervisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned training activities (scientific and transferable skills)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe planned training activities for the researcher: scientific aspects, management/organisation, horizontal and key transferable skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how training will be delivered (method, date, person), link training to career aims and objectives (SO/TO/DO), and indicate why it is important. Include a training table summarising desired skill, current level, level after training, linked objectives, means of training and responsible person. Include training activities (TA1...TAn) in the Gantt chart and include the Career Development Plan as a mandatory deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way transfer of knowledge between researcher and host
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-way transfer means mutual benefit: you will learn skills enabling your career objectives and you will bring new knowledge to the host that strengthens its research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline both directions (researcher <- host and researcher -> host). Describe what new knowledge/skills you will gain, how you will acquire them, and benefit to your career; then describe what knowledge/skills you will impart to the host, how you will impart them, and how they will be implemented. For secondments/non-academic placements/Global Fellowships, include similar detail for those partners. Summaries/tables may help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the quality and appropriateness of the researcher's existing professional experience in relation to the proposed research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise 'mini CV' highlighting research experience/results/achievements (first-author publications, specific contributions to papers, patents, prizes, international collaborations, leadership, management). Explain explicitly how your background makes you ideally suited to carry out the project and how transferable skills will ensure smooth execution. Cross-check with CV in Part B2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact: credibility of measures to enhance career perspectives and employability
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain specific measures to enhance career perspectives and employability of the researcher inside and/or outside academia and the expected contribution of proposed skills development to the researcher's future career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your career aims (where in 5-10 years), why they matter, and articulate alternative career paths. Demonstrate how the skills learned during the fellowship will make you an attractive candidate for these paths and how the fellowship contributes to MSCA expected impacts (increased research and transferable skills, improved employability).
